subject: Finishes that connect living spaces
hook: That grey looked perfect in the showroom. Then it met your floor.
ig:
That grey looked perfect in the showroom. Then it met your floor.

This is how we match finishes across rooms so they actually work in your house:

Samples go on your floor, not ours. Flooring and wall colour change how every board looks.

We check them twice: near the window and in the darkest corner. Some finishes shift a lot between the two.

Lead plus one accent. We'll usually suggest a main finish and a single accent so the living room relates to the kitchen without copying it.

Edges match faces. In the workshop the ABS edging is chosen to suit the board, so an oak-effect panel doesn't end in a white line.

Handles carry through. The same handle across rooms is the quiet bit that ties it together.

Planning furniture for an open-plan space? Send us a DM with a photo of your floor and we'll suggest a starting palette.
fb:
Ever chosen a colour that looked spot on in a showroom, then completely different at home? Light and flooring do that.

So when we help match finishes between rooms, the samples go down on your floor, get checked by the window and in the shade, and we pair one lead finish with one accent. Back in the workshop, edging is matched to the board so the colour carries round every edge.

Have a look at the furniture we make and get in touch if you'd like help pulling your rooms together.
